Per-component agreement between two lenses

Source: R/metrics.R
agreement_pairwise.Rd

Compare two lenses' parameter draws component by component, on the hub's terms. For every component the two lenses share, the table reports each lens's posterior mean and SD, the ratio of the SDs, the drift at the two reported quantiles, the Wasserstein-1 distance between the two marginals, the mean shift and the Wasserstein-1 distance expressed in reference-SD units, and the verdict those three scaled quantities imply.

Usage

agreement_pairwise(
  a,
  b,
  names = NULL,
  thresholds = agreement_thresholds(),
  sd_ref = c("max", "pooled", "a", "b")
)

Arguments

a, b

A quorum_draws() of kind "parameters", or a named list of numeric vectors in that shape.

names

Optional character vector naming the components to compare. The default compares every component the two lenses share, in a's order. Every name asked for must be present on both sides.

thresholds

A list from agreement_thresholds().

sd_ref

The reference SD the mean shift and the Wasserstein-1 distance are scaled by: "max" (the hub's larger-of-the-two, the default), "pooled" (the root-mean-square of the two), "a" or "b".

Value

A data.frame with one row per compared component and the columns param, mean_a, mean_b, sd_a, sd_b, sd_ratio, q025_diff, q975_diff, wasserstein_1, mean_shift_sd, w1_sd, verdict and reason; or a quorum_abstention() of scope "comparison" when the two lenses share no component, when a requested component is absent, or when either input is a response-curve rather than a parameter lens.

Details

The reference SD is the larger of the two posterior SDs, which is the scale the hub uses (.triangulate_verdicts, flexyBayes 0.10.0 R/triangulate.R:809: s_ref <- max(metrics$sd_a[[i]], metrics$sd_b[[i]], na.rm = TRUE)), and it is the default here so that a quorum comparison returns the same numbers the hub's comparison returned on the same draws. sd_ref offers the pooled and the one-sided scales for callers who want the comparison read against a fixed lens instead, at the cost of leaving the hub's scale.

A component with no posterior spread on either side cannot be scaled against anything, so it is reported with its raw distances, a not_compared verdict and the hub's reason string rather than a verdict the scale cannot support.

Agreement is not validation. Two lenses that share a sampler, an objective, a prior or a data-preparation step can agree because they share it; the independence ledger, not this table, is what says whether their agreement carries evidential weight.

See also

agreement_status() for the overall verdict, agreement_matrix() for a quorum of more than two lenses.

Examples

set.seed(1)
a <- list(intercept = rnorm(500L, 1, 0.5), slope = rnorm(500L, 2, 0.3))
b <- list(intercept = rnorm(500L, 1, 0.5), slope = rnorm(500L, 2.9, 0.3))
agreement_pairwise(a, b)[, c("param", "w1_sd", "verdict")]
#>       param      w1_sd    verdict
#> 1 intercept 0.05585061 concordant
#> 2     slope 2.81566274 discordant
